What kind of interview preparation should I focus on?

For a Machine Learning role, especially one involving PyTorch, your interview preparation should generally be split into three core pillars:

### 1. Technical Depth (The "How" and "Why")
*   **PyTorch Proficiency:** Don't just know the syntax. Be prepared to explain how to build custom `nn.Module` classes, how to implement custom loss functions, and how to optimize training loops (e.g., using `torch.utils.data.DataLoader`, handling GPU memory, and distributed training).
*   **Deep Learning Fundamentals:** Be ready to explain the mechanics behind architectures (Transformers, CNNs, RNNs) and optimization algorithms (Adam, SGD, learning rate schedulers). Understand the trade-offs between different activation functions and regularization techniques (Dropout, Batch Norm).
*   **ML System Design:** This is often the most critical part of senior-level interviews. You may be asked to design an end-to-end system (e.g., "How would you build a recommendation engine?"). Focus on data ingestion, feature engineering, model selection, evaluation metrics, and deployment/monitoring.

### 2. Coding & Algorithms
*   **Data Structures & Algorithms:** Even for ML roles, standard LeetCode-style questions (arrays, trees, graphs, dynamic programming) are common. Focus on medium-difficulty problems.
*   **Vectorization:** Practice writing efficient NumPy or PyTorch code. Interviewers often look for your ability to avoid explicit loops in favor of vectorized operations to improve performance.

### 3. Practical Experience & Projects
*   **The "Deep Dive":** Pick one or two projects from your resume and be prepared to discuss them in extreme detail. You should be able to explain:
    *   Why you chose a specific model architecture.
    *   How you handled data quality issues or class imbalance.
    *   How you measured success (business metrics vs. model metrics).
    *   What the biggest technical challenge was and how you overcame it.

What kind of interview preparation should I focus on?

For a Machine Learning role, especially one involving PyTorch, your interview preparation should generally be split into three core pillars:

### 1. Technical Depth (The "How" and "Why")
*   **PyTorch Proficiency:** Don't just know the syntax. Be prepared to explain how to build custom `nn.Module` classes, how to implement custom loss functions, and how to optimize training loops (e.g., using `torch.utils.data.DataLoader`, handling GPU memory, and distributed training).
*   **Deep Learning Fundamentals:** Be ready to explain the mechanics behind architectures (Transformers, CNNs, RNNs) and optimization algorithms (Adam, SGD, learning rate schedulers). Understand the trade-offs between different activation functions and regularization techniques (Dropout, Batch Norm).
*   **ML System Design:** This is often the most critical part of senior-level interviews. You may be asked to design an end-to-end system (e.g., "How would you build a recommendation engine?"). Focus on data ingestion, feature engineering, model selection, evaluation metrics, and deployment/monitoring.

### 2. Coding & Algorithms
*   **Data Structures & Algorithms:** Even for ML roles, standard LeetCode-style questions (arrays, trees, graphs, dynamic programming) are common. Focus on medium-difficulty problems.
*   **Vectorization:** Practice writing efficient NumPy or PyTorch code. Interviewers often look for your ability to avoid explicit loops in favor of vectorized operations to improve performance.

### 3. Practical Experience & Projects
*   **The "Deep Dive":** Pick one or two projects from your resume and be prepared to discuss them in extreme detail. You should be able to explain:
    *   Why you chose a specific model architecture.
    *   How you handled data quality issues or class imbalance.
    *   How you measured success (business metrics vs. model metrics).
    *   What the biggest technical challenge was and how you overcame it.
